notes.definition: A transformer is a device that changes the size of an alternating potential difference. It consists of a primary coil and a secondary coil wound on a soft iron core; the ratio of the p.d.s equals the ratio of the numbers of turns, Vp ÷ Vs = np ÷ ns.
explanation: A basic transformer has a primary coil and a secondary coil of insulated wire, wound on the same iron core. The coils are not electrically connected to each other. Iron is used for the core because it is easily magnetised (and demagnetised), so it carries a strong magnetic field from one coil to the other.

An alternating current in the primary coil produces a magnetic field in the iron core that is constantly changing in size and direction. This changing magnetic field passes through the secondary coil. A changing magnetic field around a conductor induces a potential difference across it (the generator effect), so an alternating p.d. is induced across the secondary coil. If the secondary is connected to a complete circuit, an alternating current flows. A transformer does not work with a steady d.c., because a steady current gives an unchanging field, which induces nothing.

The ratio of the potential differences across the coils depends on the ratio of the numbers of turns: Vp ÷ Vs = np ÷ ns. In a step-up transformer the secondary has more turns than the primary (ns > np), so Vs is greater than Vp. In a step-down transformer, ns < np and Vs is less than Vp. Both this equation and the power equation below are given on the equation sheet.

If a transformer is 100% efficient, the electrical power output equals the electrical power input: Vp × Ip = Vs × Is, where Vp × Ip is the input power and Vs × Is is the output power. This means that if the p.d. is stepped up, the current is stepped down by the same factor, and the other way round. You can use this to calculate the current drawn from the input supply to provide a particular power output, using Ip = power output ÷ Vp.

Transformers are essential in the National Grid. Step-up transformers at power stations increase the p.d. to very high values (such as 400 000 V) for transmission. For the same power, a higher p.d. means a much smaller current in the cables, so less energy is wasted heating the cables (power loss = I²R). This makes the system more efficient. Step-down transformers then reduce the p.d. to a safer 230 V for homes.
keyFacts: A transformer has a primary coil and a secondary coil wound on a soft iron core.
Iron is used because it is easily magnetised.
Alternating current in the primary gives a changing magnetic field in the core.
The changing field induces an alternating p.d. in the secondary coil.
Step-up: ns > np, Vs > Vp. Step-down: ns < np, Vs < Vp.
For a 100% efficient transformer, Vp × Ip = Vs × Is (equation sheet).
Stepping up the p.d. steps down the current by the same factor.
The National Grid uses high p.d. and low current to reduce energy losses in the cables.

keyTerms.definition: A device that changes the size of an alternating p.d. using two coils on an iron core.
The input coil, connected to the a.c. supply.
The output coil, across which a p.d. is induced.
A transformer with more turns on the secondary than the primary, so it increases the p.d.
A transformer with fewer turns on the secondary than the primary, so it decreases the p.d.
Soft iron on which both coils are wound; it is easily magnetised and links the changing field between the coils.
The ratio np ÷ ns of turns on the primary and secondary coils.

equations.name: Transformer turns ratio
equations.formula: p.d. across primary ÷ p.d. across secondary = turns on primary ÷ turns on secondary
equations.units: Vp and Vs in volts (V); np and ns are numbers of turns (no unit)

equations.name: Transformer power (100% efficient)
equations.formula: p.d. across primary × current in primary = p.d. across secondary × current in secondary
equations.units: V in volts (V), I in amperes (A); each side is a power in watts (W)

workedExamples.title: Finding the secondary p.d.
workedExamples.question: A transformer has 2000 turns on the primary and 100 turns on the secondary. The primary is connected to 230 V a.c. Calculate the secondary p.d.
steps: Vp ÷ Vs = np ÷ ns, so Vs = Vp × ns ÷ np.

workedExamples.title: Finding the number of turns
workedExamples.question: A transformer steps 12 V up to 240 V. The primary has 50 turns. Calculate the number of turns on the secondary.

workedExamples.title: Current in the secondary
workedExamples.question: A 100% efficient transformer has Vp = 230 V and Ip = 0.50 A. The secondary p.d. is 11.5 V. Calculate the secondary current.
steps: Vp × Ip = Vs × Is, so Is = Vp × Ip ÷ Vs.

workedExamples.title: Current drawn from the supply in kV
workedExamples.question: A 100% efficient step-up transformer at a power station has an input of 25 kV and 400 A. The output p.d. is 400 kV. Calculate the output current.
steps: Is = 25 A: the p.d. is multiplied by 16 and the current divided by 16.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think current flows through the iron core from one coil to the other.
misconceptions.right: In fact the coils are not electrically connected; energy is transferred by the changing magnetic field in the core inducing a p.d. in the secondary.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think a step-up transformer gives out more power than it takes in.
misconceptions.right: In fact a step-up transformer increases the p.d. but decreases the current; power out cannot be more than power in (Vp Ip = Vs Is at best).

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think transformers work with d.c. from a battery.
misconceptions.right: In fact a steady d.c. produces an unchanging field, which induces no p.d. in the secondary; a transformer needs a.c.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think high-voltage cables are used because they carry more current.
misconceptions.right: In fact high p.d. is used so that the current is smaller, reducing the energy wasted heating the cables.

realWorld: The National Grid uses step-up transformers at power stations and step-down transformers in substations.
Phone and laptop chargers contain step-down transformers that reduce 230 V mains to a few volts.
Electric toothbrush chargers transfer energy using the changing magnetic field between two coils, like a transformer with the core split in two.
higherTier: This whole subtopic is Higher tier only.
Explain how the effect of an alternating current in one coil in inducing a current in another is used in transformers.
Explain how the ratio of the p.d.s across the two coils depends on the ratio of the number of turns on each; calculate the current drawn from the input supply to provide a particular power output.
Apply Vp ÷ Vs = np ÷ ns and Vp × Ip = Vs × Is (both on the equation sheet); explain how transformers in the National Grid reduce power loss.
separateOnlyContent: This whole subtopic is in separate Physics (8463) only, not Combined Science (Combined students learn only that step-up and step-down transformers are used in the National Grid).
Transformer structure and operation, the turns ratio equation and the power equation for a 100% efficient transformer.
examTips: Write the equation first, then rearrange before substituting: for example Vs = Vp × ns ÷ np.
Check your answer makes sense: if ns > np, Vs must be bigger than Vp, and Is must be smaller than Ip.
Convert kV to V (× 1000) before using Vp Ip = Vs Is if the units on each side are different.
When explaining how a transformer works, mention: a.c. in primary, changing magnetic field, iron core, induced p.d. in secondary.
summary: Transformers change the size of an alternating p.d.
Two coils on a soft iron core; a.c. in the primary induces a.c. in the secondary.
Vp × Ip = Vs × Is for a 100% efficient transformer.
Step-up increases p.d. and decreases current; step-down does the reverse.
The National Grid uses high p.d., low current to reduce energy loss.

flashcards.front: What are the main parts of a transformer?
flashcards.back: A primary coil and a secondary coil wound on a soft iron core.

flashcards.front: Why is the core made of iron?
flashcards.back: Iron is easily magnetised, so it carries the changing magnetic field between the coils.

flashcards.front: Why does a transformer need a.c.?
flashcards.back: Only a changing current gives a changing magnetic field, which induces a p.d. in the secondary.

flashcards.front: Power equation for a 100% efficient transformer
What does a step-up transformer do?
flashcards.back: Increases the p.d. (ns > np) and decreases the current.

flashcards.front: What does a step-down transformer do?
flashcards.back: Decreases the p.d. (ns < np) and increases the current.

flashcards.front: Why does the National Grid transmit at high p.d.?
flashcards.back: For the same power the current is lower, so less energy is wasted heating the cables.

flashcards.front: Rearrange Vp ÷ Vs = np ÷ ns for Vs.
How do you calculate the current drawn from the supply?
flashcards.back: Ip = power output ÷ Vp (for a 100% efficient transformer).

flashcards.front: Are the primary and secondary coils electrically connected?
flashcards.back: No; they are linked only by the changing magnetic field in the core.
The input power to the transformer.

markScheme: 1 mark: Soft iron
questions.explanation: Soft iron is easily magnetised, so it carries the changing magnetic field from the primary to the secondary coil.

questions.question: What does a step-up transformer do to the potential difference?
markScheme: 1 mark: Increases it
questions.explanation: A step-up transformer has more turns on the secondary, so the output p.d. is larger than the input.

questions.question: In a step-down transformer, how do the numbers of turns compare?
options: More turns on the secondary than the primary
Fewer turns on the secondary than the primary
markScheme: 1 mark: Fewer turns on the secondary than the primary
questions.explanation: Fewer secondary turns gives a smaller secondary p.d., because Vs ÷ Vp = ns ÷ np.

questions.question: Why does a transformer not work with a steady d.c. supply?
options: A steady current gives an unchanging magnetic field, which induces no p.d.
markScheme: 1 mark: A steady current gives an unchanging magnetic field, which induces no p.d.
questions.explanation: A p.d. is only induced by a changing field. Steady d.c. gives a constant field, so nothing is induced in the secondary (except briefly at switch-on or off).

questions.question: A transformer steps up the p.d. by a factor of 10. If it is 100% efficient, what happens to the current?
options: It increases by a factor of 10
It decreases by a factor of 10
It decreases by a factor of 100
markScheme: 1 mark: It decreases by a factor of 10
questions.explanation: Vp Ip = Vs Is, so if V is multiplied by 10, I is divided by 10 to keep the power the same.

To make the electricity travel faster
markScheme: 1 mark: To reduce the current and so reduce energy losses in the cables
questions.explanation: For a given power, a higher p.d. means a smaller current, and the heating loss depends on I²R.

questions.question: What happens in the secondary coil of a transformer?
options: A current flows directly from the primary through the core
The magnetic field is converted into heat only
An alternating p.d. is induced by the changing magnetic field
markScheme: 1 mark: An alternating p.d. is induced by the changing magnetic field
questions.explanation: The changing field in the core passes through the secondary coil and induces an alternating p.d.

questions.question:
Table 1 shows information about a transformer.
The transformer is 100% efficient.
What are the p.d. across the secondary coil and the current in the secondary coil?
markScheme: 1 mark: 60 V and 2.0 A
questions.explanation: Vs = 240 × 100 ÷ 400 = 60 V. Power in = 240 × 0.50 = 120 W, so Is = 120 ÷ 60 = 2.0 A. Stepping down the p.d. steps up the current.

questions.question: Which change would increase the output p.d. of a step-down transformer, with the same input?
options: Replacing the iron core with plastic
markScheme: 1 mark: Adding turns to the secondary
questions.explanation: Vs = Vp × ns ÷ np: increasing ns increases Vs. Adding primary turns decreases Vs; a plastic core weakens the field link.

questions.question: Why are real transformers slightly less than 100% efficient?
options: Some energy is dissipated heating the coils and core
The current in the secondary is always zero
The iron core is not magnetic
markScheme: 1 mark: Some energy is dissipated heating the coils and core
questions.explanation: The coils have resistance and the core heats up as it is repeatedly magnetised, so output power is slightly less than input power.

questions.question:
A transformer increases a p.d. from 12 V to 240 V.
The primary coil has 50 turns.
Calculate the number of turns on the secondary coil.
Use the equation:
p.d. across primary coil ÷ p.d. across secondary coil = number of turns on primary coil ÷ number of turns on secondary coil
questions.answerLabel: Number of turns on secondary coil
markScheme: 1 mark: ns = 1000
questions.explanation: ns = np × Vs ÷ Vp = 50 × 240 ÷ 12 = 1000 turns.

questions.question:
Table 1 shows information about a transformer.
The transformer is 100% efficient.
Calculate the current in the secondary coil.
Use the equation:

markScheme: 1 mark: Vp Ip = Vs Is

questions.question:
A transformer supplies a 12 V, 60 W lamp from the 230 V mains supply.
The transformer is 100% efficient.
Calculate the current drawn from the mains supply.
Give your answer to 2 significant figures.
markScheme: 1 mark: power output = power input = 60 W
1 mark: Ip = 60 ÷ 230
1 mark: Ip = 0.26 A
questions.explanation: Vp Ip = Vs Is = 60 W, so Ip = 60 ÷ 230 = 0.261 A. The lamp current (5.0 A) is much larger than the mains current.

questions.question:
A step-up transformer at a power station is 100% efficient.
Table 1 shows information about the transformer.
Calculate the output current.
Use the equation:
p.d. across primary coil × current in primary coil = p.d. across secondary coil × current in secondary coil
markScheme: 1 mark: Is = Vp Ip ÷ Vs
1 mark: Is = 25 A
questions.explanation: The p.d. increases 16 times, so the current falls 16 times: 400 ÷ 16 = 25 A. Using kV on both sides gives the same answer because the units cancel.

questions.question:
A phone charger contains a transformer that reduces 230 V to 5.0 V.
The secondary coil has 40 turns.
Calculate the number of turns on the primary coil.
Use the equation:
p.d. across primary coil ÷ p.d. across secondary coil = number of turns on primary coil ÷ number of turns on secondary coil
questions.answerLabel: Number of turns on primary coil
markScheme: 1 mark: np = ns × Vp ÷ Vs
1 mark: np = 1840
questions.explanation: np ÷ ns = Vp ÷ Vs, so np = 40 × 230 ÷ 5.0 = 1840 turns.

questions.question:
A transmission cable has a resistance of 10 Ω.
Table 1 shows two values of the current in the cable.
Calculate how many times smaller the power wasted in the cable is when the current is 25 A instead of 400 A.
Use the equation:
power = current² × resistance
markScheme: 1 mark: power loss = I²R
1 mark: ratio = 256
questions.explanation: Power loss = I²R. 1 600 000 ÷ 6250 = 256, which is (400 ÷ 25)² = 16². Reducing the current 16 times reduces losses 256 times.

questions.question: Give the reason the core of a transformer is made of iron.
markScheme: 1 mark: iron is easily magnetised (and demagnetised)
questions.explanation: This lets the changing magnetic field pass strongly from one coil to the other.

questions.question: Explain how an alternating current in the primary coil of a transformer produces an alternating p.d. across the secondary coil.
markScheme: 1 mark: the alternating current produces a changing (alternating) magnetic field
1 mark: the iron core carries this changing field through the secondary coil
1 mark: the changing field induces an alternating p.d. across the secondary coil
questions.explanation: This is the generator effect: a changing field around a conductor induces a p.d.

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows how electricity is transmitted through the National Grid.
Explain how the step-up transformer reduces energy losses.

1 mark: a smaller current means less energy is wasted heating the cables (power loss = I²R)
questions.explanation: Lower current means less heating, so the system is more efficient.

questions.question: A student says that a step-up transformer is a way of getting more energy out than you put in. Explain why this is wrong.
markScheme: 1 mark: power output cannot be more than power input (energy is conserved); at best Vp Ip = Vs Is
1 mark: the p.d. increases but the current decreases by the same factor
questions.explanation: A transformer changes the balance of p.d. and current, not the total power.

questions.question: Suggest why step-down transformers are needed before electricity reaches homes.
markScheme: 1 mark: transmission p.d.s (hundreds of kV) are extremely dangerous
1 mark: so the p.d. is reduced to a safer 230 V for use in homes (and appliances are designed for 230 V)
questions.explanation: High p.d. is efficient for transmission but unsafe for domestic use.

questions.question: Describe the structure of a basic transformer and explain why it only works with alternating current.
markScheme: Indicative content: primary coil and secondary coil of insulated wire; both wound on the same soft iron core; coils not electrically connected; iron is easily magnetised; a.c. in the primary produces a changing magnetic field in the core; changing field passes through the secondary and induces a p.d.; d.c. produces a steady field which does not change, so no p.d. is induced.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): clear description of the structure with a correct explanation of the need for a.c.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): names parts or states a.c. is needed, with little explanation.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: The key physics is that only a changing magnetic field induces a p.d.

questions.question:

Table 1 shows data for a power station and the step-up transformer connected to it.
Use calculations to support your answer.
